claim: Discovery script classified all 9 raw relations from source-records.json, correctly rejecting 1 stale edge, 1 missing-target edge, and 1 unreachable-source edge.
proves: Shows the discovery script processes the complete raw edge set, not a partial subset.
does_not_prove: Does not prove correctness against a different variant's edge count or shape.
alternative_considered: Only classify BFS-reached edges (original version); rejected because it silently dropped the unreachable AdminTo edge, undercounting validated edges.
disposition: Kept the full-classification version; documented the fix in decision-log.md D-002.

claim: Discovery script correctly identified both attack paths (foothold to archive-primary via WriteSPN+ReadProof; foothold to archive-secondary via GenericAll+ReadProof) with no hardcoded object names.
proves: Shows path discovery logic reads object type and relation data at runtime rather than matching literal names.
does_not_prove: Does not prove behavior against a variant with a different graph shape (e.g. 3+ hop chains).
alternative_considered: Manual trace of the graph by hand (done first, in chat, before scripting).
disposition: Automated version retained as the scored deliverable; manual trace used only to validate script correctness.

claim: Path 1 automation (set-spn -> request-service-token -> read-proof-1 -> cleanup) succeeded 3 of 3 times from a clean checkpoint, with real proof value verified against candidate.json each time.
proves: Shows the automation is reliable and reproducible from a clean state, not a one-off success.
does_not_prove: Does not prove behavior under concurrent range access or a different candidate variant.
alternative_considered: Single manual run without repetition; rejected since the brief requires proof of 3x reliability, not a single success.
disposition: Automated 3x loop with per-attempt proof verification kept as the scored method.

claim: Path 2 automation (add-group-member -> read-proof-2 -> cleanup) succeeded 3 of 3 times from a clean checkpoint, with real proof value verified against candidate.json each time.
proves: Shows Path 2 automation is independently reliable and reproducible.
does_not_prove: Does not prove this path is distinct in mechanism from Path 1 by itself - see C-001/C-002 for the ACL-only vs credential-abuse distinction.
alternative_considered: n/a - only one viable sequence exists for this edge type in the tool's act interface.

claim: Applying remediate-path-1 causes the identical Path 1 sequence to fail at its intended first step (set-spn), while range health remains green afterward.
proves: Shows the fix blocks the attack at the correct edge without breaking the range's overall health.
does_not_prove: Does not prove the fix would hold against a different attack technique targeting the same account.
alternative_considered: Testing remediation by only checking the final read-proof-1 step failed, rather than the first blocked step.
disposition: Chose to assert the block occurs at the intended first edge (set-spn), matching the brief's 'fail at its intended edge' requirement precisely.

claim: Applying remediate-path-2 causes the identical Path 2 sequence to fail at its intended first step (add-group-member), while range health remains green afterward.
proves: Shows the fix blocks the attack at the correct edge without breaking the range's overall health.
does_not_prove: Does not prove the fix would hold against a different attack technique targeting the same group.
alternative_considered: n/a - single viable blocking point exists in the tool's remediation interface.

claim: Detection rule spn_abuse_chain alerts on the real Path 1 attack sequence and on a synthetic positive fixture, but does not alert on a synthetic benign SPN-rotation fixture with an incomplete chain.
exact_locator: JSON path /detections/0/alert = true (real data); detection-test-results.txt positive-spn-abuse.jsonl and benign-spn-rotation.jsonl entries
proves: Shows the rule fires on genuine attack activity and stays silent on a plausible legitimate-looking partial action.
does_not_prove: Does not prove behavior against a benign fixture that completes the full 3-step chain for a legitimate business reason.
alternative_considered: Testing only against synthetic fixtures without real captured data.
disposition: Added the real-data confirmation run specifically to strengthen this claim beyond fixture-only evidence.
